turns.thought:
Yes — turn Airplane Mode off. That would fully explain what you're seeing.

**Why This Is the Cause**

Airplane Mode disables *all* your phone's wireless radios — cellular, Wi-Fi, and Bluetooth — at once. That's exactly why you're seeing no signal bars and no network indicator, even though your line is active and healthy on our end.

This also lines up with everything I confirmed on your account: your line **555-123-2002 is Active**, the suspension is cleared, and your **$65.00 payment went through**. Nothing on your account is blocking service. Airplane Mode being switched on is almost certainly what's left.

**What To Do**

1. **On your phone, open Settings and toggle Airplane Mode to OFF.**
   - *(On most phones you can also swipe down from the top of the screen to open Quick Settings and tap the airplane icon to turn it off.)*
2. **Wait about 30 seconds** and watch the status bar.
3. You should see the airplane icon disappear and your **signal bars return**, along with a network type like **5G**, **LTE**, or **4G**.

Once the airplane icon is gone, try making a quick call or loading a webpage to confirm everything works.

Let me know what you see after turning it off — if the signal bars don't come back, there are a few other things on the device side we can check, and I'll walk you through them.

I hear you — you've done everything asked of you, so let me be clear about where things stand and get you to the finish line.

**Your Account Is Fully Clear (I Just Re-Verified Everything)**

- **Line 555-123-2002:** Active ✅
- **Bill B1234321 ($65.00):** Paid ✅
- **Contract:** Valid through Dec 31, 2026 ✅
- **Other bills:** No other overdue balances blocking you ✅
- **Data:** 8.7 GB of 15 GB used ✅

So there is **nothing on the carrier side** stopping your service. The remaining cause is on the phone itself — which is actually good news, because it's fixable.

**Two Useful Clues**

You mentioned the status bar shows **"Data Disabled."** That's separate from your signal problem — it means the mobile data switch itself is turned off in your phone's settings, and it won't turn itself back on. The **"No Signal"** is the other half, and it points to how the phone is trying to connect.

**Please Try These In Order**

1. **Turn Mobile Data back ON.** Go to **Settings → Network & Internet → Mobile Network** and switch **Mobile Data ON**. (On most phones you can also swipe down from the top and tap the Mobile Data tile.)
2. **Reseat your SIM card.** Power the phone off, remove the SIM, wait a few seconds, reinsert it firmly, and power back on. A loosely seated SIM is a very common cause of "No Signal" after a reboot.
3. **Check your network mode.** In the same Mobile Network menu, look for **Preferred network mode**. If it's set to **2G or 3G only**, change it to **4G/5G preferred** (sometimes labeled "5G/LTE"). Older modes can leave you with no usable signal.
4. **Reset your APN settings, then reboot.** In Mobile Network settings, find **Access Point Names (APN)**, choose **Reset to default** from the menu, then **restart your phone**. APN settings are required for the phone to attach to the network at all — and they only take effect after a reboot.

After step 4, give the phone about a minute and watch the status bar for your signal bars and a network type like **5G**, **LTE**, or **4G**.

**If It's Still Dead After That**

Don't keep troubleshooting on your own — we'll bring in a specialist. Just say the word and I'll transfer you directly to technical support, and I'll pass along everything we've already done (the paid bill, the cleared suspension, and these steps) so you won't have to repeat yourself.

Let me know what the status bar shows after you try those.

**Do this first: turn Mobile Data back ON.**

2. Tap **Network & Internet** (on some phones it's called **Connections**).
3. Tap **Mobile Network**.
4. Toggle **Mobile Data** to **ON**.

*Quick alternative:* swipe down from the top of your screen to open Quick Settings and tap the **Mobile Data** tile so it's no longer grayed out.

**Important expectation-setting:** this will fix the **"Data Disabled"** message, but it probably will **not** bring back your signal bars. "No Signal" and "Data Disabled" are two separate issues — mobile data can't work until the phone connects to the network, and right now it isn't connecting at all.

So after you do this, you should see the **"Data Disabled"** message disappear from the status bar, and you may still see **"No Signal."** If that happens, **don't worry — that's expected**, and we move on to the next step.

Turn mobile data on now, and tell me what the status bar says afterward. Then I'll give you the single next step to try.

Yes — toggle it one more time. That toggle is a switch: it flips to whatever the opposite of the current state is, so if it just reported **OFF**, tapping it once more should flip it to **ON**.

**Do this: toggle Mobile Data one more time** (same place as before), then look at the status bar.

But here's the rule so you don't get stuck in a loop:

- **If it now says "Mobile Data is now ON"** and the "Data Disabled" message disappears — great, that step is done. Tell me, and I'll give you the next single step.
- **If it says "OFF" again, or the status bar still shows "Data Disabled"** — stop toggling. Don't repeat it a third time. Just tell me and we'll move on.

**Why I say don't keep repeating it:** turning data on can't create signal. Your phone has to be connected to the network first before mobile data means anything, and right now it's showing **"No Signal"** — it isn't connected at all. That's the real thing we need to fix, and mobile data isn't the lever for it.

So if this second toggle doesn't take, the very next thing we'll do is **reseat your SIM card** — that directly targets the "No Signal" problem and is the most likely fix at this point.

Try the toggle once and let me know exactly what it reports and what the status bar shows.

Good — mobile data is ON now on your end. The status bar hasn't caught up yet because there's still no network connection for it to attach to, which is exactly what we expected. That step is done; let's move on to the actual "No Signal" cause.

**Next step: reseat your SIM card.**

A SIM that isn't making solid contact with the phone is one of the most common reasons for "No Signal" — and it makes sense here, since your SIM was replaced on Jan 20 and your line was suspended/resumed today.

1. **Power your phone completely OFF.**
2. **Remove the SIM card.** Use the SIM eject tool (or a small paperclip) in the tiny hole on the side or top edge of your phone. Pull the tray out gently.
3. **Wait about 10 seconds**, then **reseat the card** — make sure it's lying flat and snug in the tray, not tilted or loose.
4. **Push the tray back in firmly** until it's flush with the phone.
5. **Power the phone back ON.**
6. **Wait about a minute**, then check the status bar.

**What to look for:** the airplane icon gone, and your **signal bars** appearing with a network type like **5G**, **LTE**, or **4G** alongside it.
